fullPassage: A "complementary good" is a product that is often consumed alongside another product. For example, popcorn is a complementary good to a movie, while a travel pillow is a complementary good for a long plane journey. When the popularity of one product increases, the sales of its complementary good also increase. By producing goods that complement other products that are already (or about to be) popular, you can ensure a steady stream of demand for your product. Some products enjoy perfect complementary status — they have to be consumed together, such as a lamp and a lightbulb. However, do not assume that a product is perfectly complementary, as customers may not be completely locked in to the product. For example, although motorists may seem required to purchase gasoline to run their cars, they can switch to electric cars.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 locked in to the product가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 'locked in to the product(그 제품에 묶여 있는)'는 소비자가 그 제품에서 벗어나 다른 것으로 바꾸지 못하는 상태를 비유한다.
det.analysis:

❌ ② physically trapped inside a store(가게 안에 물리적으로 갇힌): locked을 물리적 감금으로 오해한 함정

❌ ③ legally banned from buying the product(그 제품 구매가 법적으로 금지된): 법적 금지 이야기가 아님

❌ ④ given a lifetime discount on the product(평생 할인을 받는): 본문에 없는 내용
det.tip: locked in = 다른 제품으로 갈아타지 못하고 매여 있음

questions.passage: A "complementary good" is a product that is often consumed alongside another product. For example, popcorn is a complementary good to a movie, while a travel pillow is a complementary good for a long plane journey. When the popularity of one product increases, the sales of its complementary good also increase. By producing goods that complement other products that are already (or about to be) popular, you can ensure a steady stream of demand for your product. Some products enjoy perfect complementary status — they have to be consumed together, such as a lamp and a lightbulb. However, do not assume that a product is perfectly complementary, as customers may not be completely locked in to the product. For example, although motorists may seem required to purchase gasoline to run <u>their</u> cars, they can switch to electric cars.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 their가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: their는 앞에 언급된 motorists(운전자들)를 가리킨다. '그들의 차(their cars)'를 굴리기 위해 휘발유가 필요하다는 맥락이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 자동차들: their의 수식을 받는 대상(cars)이지 가리키는 대상이 아님

❌ ② 전기차들: 뒤 문장에 나오는 대안으로, their가 가리키는 것이 아님

❌ ③ 보완재들: 소유 주체가 될 수 없음

✅ ④ 운전자들(motorists) ←정답: 'motorists may seem required to purchase gasoline to run their cars'에서 their = 앞의 motorists
